Journal.Title: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society

Article.ArticleTitle: Serum IgA/C3 and glomerular C3 staining predict severity of IgA nephropathy.

Abstract.AbstractText: We evaluated whether the serum IgA/C3 ratio and glomerular C3 staining predict prognosis in IgA nephropathy.

We collected data for 44 IgA nephropathy children treated with multi-drug combination therapy. The children were retrospectively divided into four groups based on the serum IgA/C3 ratio and glomerular C3 staining. Group A consisted of 9 children with a higher than median IgA/C3 ratio and glomerular C3 staining ≧2.0, Group B consisted of 7 children with a higher than median IgA/C3 ratio and glomerular C3 staining <2.0, Group C consisted of 7 children with a lower than median IgA/C3 ratio and glomerular C3 staining ≧2.0, and Group D consisted of 21 children with a lower than median IgA/C3 ratio and glomerular C3 staining <2.0. The clinical features, pathological findings at the first and second renal biopsies as well as at the latest follow-up, and prognosis were analyzed for the four groups.

At the most recent follow-up, the urinary protein excretion, incidence of hematuria, and serum creatinine levels in Group A were all higher those in Group D. At the second biopsy, the ratio of the absence/presence of crescents, MESTCG score, and CI in Group A were higher than those in Group D. All patients in Group D had normal urine, and the frequency of patients with persistent nephropathy in Group A was higher than that in Group D.
Our result suggested that serum IgA/C3 ratio and glomerular C3 staining can predict prognosis in IgA nephropathy. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
